Plant Almanac plant: Tomato - Sweet 1000.
Scientific name: Solanum lycopersicum.
Family: Solanaceae.
Summary: Tomato recorded as Sweet 1000. The cultivar name islisted by a supplier; the growing guidance here is for tomatoes generally until the seed-packet identity is confirmed..
Water needs: moderate.
Sun needs: full sun.
Care: Sydney /warm-temperate guidance. General tomato guidance: provide full sun, steady soil moisture and support appropriate to the plant’s habit. Allow 90 cm between plants and 150 cm between rows as a roomy planning layout. Planning estimates: in row spacing cm, row spacing cm, soil ph min, soil ph max, feeder type, water needs, sun needs, forest layer..
Sowing notes: Sydney / warm temperate: sow August–December using general tomato guidance from Eden’s mild-climate calendar. Start early sowings under protection and transplant after frost risk. Not a verified Sweet 1000 calendar..
Recorded planting months: August, September, October, November, December.
Minimum soil pH: 5.5.
Maximum soil pH: 7.0.
In-row spacing (cm): 90.0.
Row spacing (cm): 150.0.
Yield notes: Pick ripe fruit as it develops. Generic tomato guidance suggests about 65–90 days from transplanting to first harvest, but Sweet 1000 maturity, crop duration and yield remain unverified..
Feeder type: heavy feeder.
Forest layer: herbaceous.
Part used: fruit.
Uses: culinary.
Uses notes: Use ripe tomato fruit fresh or cooked. The record is kept separate from Sweet 100 and Sweet Million; fruit size and flavour are not assumed..
Management notes: Mulch, water evenly and allow airflow. Rotate away from other nightshade crops. Spacing, feeding, water, pH, layer and calendar are species-level guidance, not verified cultivar traits..
Recorded reference source:https://www.hrseeds.com/pepper-and-tomato-seed-list.
Rotation group: Solanums; feeder weight: heavy; rotation exempt: False.

Plant Almanac plant: Tomato - Black Krim.
Scientific name: Solanum lycopersicum.
Summary: Dark slicing tomato for warm-season growing with a sturdy stake or cage..
Water needs: high.
Sun needs: full sun.
Care: Provide a sturdy stake or cage and tie stems loosely as the plant grows..
Sowing notes: Aug–Dec.
Minimum soil pH: 6.0.
Maximum soil pH: 7.0.
In-row spacing (cm): 50.0.
Row spacing (cm): 80.0.
Harvest window (weeks): 10.0.
Yield per plant: 3.0.
Yield unit: kg.
Yield notes: 3 kg per established plantover a 10-week harvest window. Total across repeated pickings, not the yield at every picking..
Feeder type: heavy feeder.
Forest layer: herbaceous.
Part used: fruit.
Uses: culinary.
Uses notes: Tall summer crop; keep lower-growing companions outside its main root and shade area.
Fresh in salads, roasted, or cooked into sauces and relishes..
Management notes: Inspect weekly, remove affected plant material, use clean tools and encourage beneficial insects. Confirm the pest or disease before choosing treatment..
Associated pests: Aphids, Slugs and snails.
Rotation group: Solanums; feeder weight: heavy; rotation exempt: False.
Recorded companion: Basil - Genovese; function: pollinator attractor; notes: Grow on the sunny side with room for both plants. Let a few basil stems flower to provide nectar for visiting insects..
Recorded companion: Marigold - French Marigold; function: pollinator attractor; notes: Add a sunny flowering border for insect habitat. Leave enough space between the flowers and the crop for light and airflow..

Plant Almanac disease: Tomato early blight.
Brown leaf spots with concentric rings can develop, often on older tomato leaves. Check: Inspect spot patterns and compare a tomato-specific reference; do not identify from yellowing alone. First actions: Remove affected debris, reduce soil splash and provide spacing and crop rotation. Similar-looking problems: Septoria leaf spot; other blights; nutrient problems. These signs suggest possibilities, not a confirmed diagnosis.
